questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Matters
This question assesses your understanding of certificate rotation, CSR workflows, SPIFFE identities, and tenant isolation in Kubernetes-based CNF (Cloud-Native Function) gateway platforms. It validates your ability to design lifecycle management solutions that operate without downtime and your competence in developing testable configurations before production rollout.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant CSR issuance within Kubernetes
- Rotating CA with short-lived certificates for enhanced security
- SPIFFE identities and TLS handshakes in multi-tenant CNF gateways
- Tenant isolation using separate namespaces

## Solution Architecture

### 1. Minimal CA Manifest

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca
  namespace: cnf-gateway
type: kubernetes.io/tls
data:
  ca.crt: <base64-encoded-CA-certificate>
  ca.key: <base64-encoded-CA-private-key>
```

### 2. CSR Flow and Approval Policy

```yaml
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-csr
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  groups:
  - system:authenticated
  request: <base64-encoded-CSR>
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-client
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
---
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-csr
spec:
  approval:
  - user: system:controller:certificates-approver
    approval: true
  conditions:
  - type: Approved
    reason: TenantIdentityValidated
    message: CSR identity matches tenant namespace
```

### 3. Per-Tenant CA Rotation Policy (30-Day Renewal)

```yaml
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: tenant-ca-issuer
  namespace: cnf-gateway
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: tenant-ca
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: gateway-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: gateway-tls
  issuerRef:
    name: tenant-ca-issuer
    kind: Issuer
  commonName: gateway.tenant-a.cnf
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.cnf
  spiffeURIs:
  - spiffe://cnf/tenant-a/gateway
  duration: 720h # 30 days
  renewBefore: 168h # 7 days before expiry
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
  - server auth
```

### 4. Test Manifest with Sidecar Validation

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  labels:
    tenant-id: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 8443
    targetPort: 8443
  selector:
    app: gateway
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: cnf-gateway:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls-certs
          mountPath: /etc/tls
          readOnly: true
        env:
        - name: SPIFFE_ID
          value: spiffe://cnf/tenant-a/gateway
      volumes:
      - name: tls-certs
        secret:
          secretName: gateway-tls
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test-validator
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  restartPolicy: Never
  containers:
  - name: validator
    image: curl:latest
    command: ["sh", "-c"]
    args:
    - |
      # Validate TLS handshake
      openssl s_client -connect gateway:8443 \
        -CAfile /etc/tls/ca.crt \
        -cert /etc/tls/tls.crt \
        -key /etc/tls/tls.key \
        -verify_return_error
    volumeMounts:
    - name: tls-certs
      mountPath: /etc/tls
      readOnly: true
  volumes:
  - name: tls-certs
    secret:
      secretName: gateway-tls
```

### 5. SPIFFE Identity Validation

Each tenant receives a SPIFFE identity in the format `spiffe://cnf/{tenant}/gateway`. The CSR approval policy validates that the requested identity matches the tenant's namespace before issuance, ensuring strict tenant isolation.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question assesses real-world upgrade discipline in cloud-native networking functions (CNF): zero-downtime deployments, per-tenant TLS key rotation, and reliable KMS-backed certificate flows—all in a multi-tenant Kubernetes environment.

## Key Concepts
- Canary rollouts with per-namespace traffic control using progressive traffic shifting
- CSR-based TLS rotation via an in-cluster KMS-backed Certificate Authority
- TenantRotation CRD to trigger cross-namespace certificate refresh
- Readiness probes with TLS handshake validation during upgrades
- Traffic shadows for testing new versions without affecting production

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example 1: Deployment rolling update strategy
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxSurge: 1
      maxUnavailable: 0
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
        version: v1.y
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8443
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        env:
        - name: KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST
          value: "kubernetes.default.svc"
        - name: VAULT_ADDR
          value: "http://vault-in-cluster:8200"
```

```yaml
# Example 2: TenantRotation CRD for per-tenant TLS rotation
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Certificate
metadata:
  name: tenant-mtls-cert
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  secretName: tenant-a-mtls-secret
  duration: 24h
  renewBefore: 12h
  issuerRef:
    name: kms-tenant-issuer
    kind: ClusterIssuer
  dnsNames:
  - gateway.tenant-a.svc.cluster.local
  commonName: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: security.example.com/v1
kind: TenantRotation
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rotation
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenantNamespace: tenant-a
  certificateRef:
    name: tenant-mtls-cert
  rotationStrategy: rolling
  preRotationValidation:
    enabled: true
    timeout: 30s
```

```yaml
# Example 3: Minimal one-namespace test manifest
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: test-tenant
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: test-ca-key
  namespace: test-tenant
type: Opaque
data:
  ca.key: <base64-encoded-key>
---
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: test-ca-issuer
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  ca:
    secretName: test-ca-key
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway-test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: gateway:v1.y
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
        env:
        - name: TENANT_NAMESPACE
          value: test-tenant
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8443
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: gateway-test
  namespace: test-tenant
spec:
  selector:
    app: gateway-test
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8443
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests real-world per-tenant canary strategies, traffic splitting, and rollback logic under latency and error constraints.

## Key Concepts

- Canary rollout with per-tenant isolation
- Prometheus metric-driven analysis
- Rollout/VirtualService integration
- Safe rollback and promotion windows

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-rollout
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/org/gateway:canary
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 900s }
      - setWeight: 100
```

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: VirtualService
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  http:
  - route:

        host: gateway
        subset: stable
      weight: 90
    - destination:
        host: gateway
        subset: canary
      weight: 10
```

Tests the ability to add a safety net for idempotent requests in a multi-tenant gateway, with backends and observability considerations.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant dedup caches
- Safe idempotent handling via X-Request-ID
- TTL-based eviction and TTL refresh on success
- Pluggable backends (Redis or memory)

## Code Example
```javascript
// sample pseudo-logic for dedup check
const key = `${tenantId}|${path}|${requestId}`;
if (cache.has(key)) return respond(409);
cache.set(key, true, ttlSeconds);
forwardRequest();
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test race conditions with concurrent requests?
- How would you migrate from in-memory to Redis without downtime?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests real-world operations: key rotation, SBOM integrity, policy enforcement in multi-tenant CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant key management with Cosign and KMS/Vault
- SBOM regeneration on rotation
- Admission control with ImagePolicyWebhook/OPA
- Namespace-scoped validation and rollback

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example OPA policy fragment enforcing signature and SBOM for CNF images
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: cnf-image-policy
  namespace: default
data:
  policy.rego: |
    package cnf.image
    default allow = false
    allow {
      input.request.kind == "ImageReview"
      input.request.object.spec.containers[_].image
      ...
    }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle cross-tenant key revocation and audit?
- How do you ensure SBOM provenance for multi-arch images?
